W2-1.summary: With the thread executor off, an injected sequential timing executor gives the same fire sequence as the analysis run on every rep, and its count-based numbers match C3, C7 and C10 exactly. Q1: under D.2's per-cell home rule at K=8 the busiest executor holds 0.986/0.967 of fire time on the two heavy files, which is worse than by count (0.893/0.847). Q2: per-component ownership fixes balance, with the busiest share by time about 1/K (0.14 at K=8). It does not give speedup: time-weighted parallelism per round is 1.19/1.35 at K=8. The cap is the dependency structure, not the ownership unit: work/span is 1.28/1.49, and homing by propagator id hits the same ceiling. Q3: per-component fencing (only :type and type cells) still fences 85–92% of fire time; per-cell fencing fences 97–99%. D.2's alternation needs at most 2 switches per S0 run (mean 1.44–1.55, at most 1 on the critical path), so C9-11's 'as many syncs as BSP rounds' does not hold on the corpus. Q4: 6 of the 17 medium-tier files run no BSP S0 at all, and across the 17 the S0 fire time is 1.47 ms out of 127 ms of commands (1.2%); the relational and solver files run about one fire per S0 run. Verdict: P3 has no workload in this repo under any ownership unit. The zero-overhead bound is ≤1.05–1.06× on the heavy-file commands without a fence and ≤1.01× with D.2's fence at either granularity. So C10-6's deferral holds and D2P-5 selects the whole-network rule (i).

verdicts.question: Q1. Under D.2's per-cell home rule (a fire runs on the owner of its first output; round-robin; K=8), is the busiest executor's share by fire time ≥ 0.8 on the two heavy files?
verdicts.amendment: Measured by time the share is higher than by count: 0.986–0.987 (constraints-adversarial) and 0.965–0.969 (type-adversarial), against 0.893/0.847 by count. The fires homed elsewhere (meta-solution, classify-inhabit-request, resolution cells) are the cheap ones: p50 fire 1 µs, p90 23–34 µs. Effective parallelism per round by time is 1.01/1.02 at K = 4, 8 and 16. Fire time includes BSP's per-fire collect step (fire-and-collect-writes, propagator.rkt:2876-2983).
verdicts.evidence: MEASUREMENT. Probe gran-probe.rkt, which injects a timing executor through current-parallel-executor (propagator.rkt:3675, called at :3497) making the same calls as sequential-fire-all (:3295). Command: timeout -k 10 900 racket benchmarks/par4/hold-suite-lock.rkt tools/suite-lock.rkt /bin/bash lockrun.sh, i.e. 3 interleaved runs per heavy file, each with 7 timing reps. Fire time is the per-fire median over the reps. Suite lock held exclusively; load 3.44→3.65 on 18 cores (6P+12E). Output (ranges over the 3 runs): constraints-adversarial: 1136 fires, S0 fire 10.02–10.44 ms; CELL K=8 busiest count 0.893, time 0.986–0.987. type-adversarial: 1140 fires, 7.32–7.54 ms; count 0.847, time 0.965–0.969. Rule source: D.2 §6.7 (2026-10-15_PAR_4_D2_DESIGN.md:305).
verdicts.power_check: Calibration: the count-based numbers reproduce C3 and C10 exactly (0.893/0.847; implicit-args 0.867, matching C3's 0.8667). The per-round count parallelism for width ≥2 matches C7: 1.11/1.13 at K=8. The same instrument with homing by propagator id gives a busiest share of 0.140–0.162 by time, so it reports balance where balance exists. All 7 timing reps reproduce the analysed fire sequence (rep_seq_match all true). Across the 3 locked runs the time shares move by ≤0.003.

verdicts.question: Q2. Under per-component ownership (component = (position, facet); home = owner of the first component written, from the delta keys or the declared #:component-paths), what are the busiest share by time and the effective parallelism at K ∈ {4,8,16}? Does it restore the parallelism the K>1 models assume (CL-1's direction)?
verdicts.amendment: Per-component ownership removes the hub imbalance but not the limit on speedup. Busiest share by time at K=4/8/16: constraints 0.264/0.143–0.146/0.088–0.093; type 0.267–0.270/0.141–0.147/0.094–0.100. That is about 1/K, the same as the power row. Effective parallelism per round, by count: 2.12/3.12/3.61 and 2.32/3.11/3.67. By time: 1.15/1.19–1.20/1.22–1.23 and 1.29–1.30/1.34–1.35/1.39–1.40. The asynchronous bound with zero overhead, max(span, busiest load) per run, is 1.26–1.28 and 1.46–1.49 at every K. That equals work/span, so the dependency chain binds and the ownership unit does not. Why: in each round one heavy :type fire holds 79%/69% of the round's time, only 16 of 214 and 20 of 185 rounds have two or more fires over 20 µs, and the top decile of fires holds 72% of the time. The static rule (write profile, otherwise the declared #:component-paths, used for 617/631 fires) agrees with the post-hoc delta rule to within 0.01. Homing components by hash instead of first-seen order changes nothing material. The models assumed 4.07×/3.26× at K=8 (D.2 §2 item 3).
verdicts.evidence: MEASUREMENT. Same probe and runs as Q1; analysis gran_analyze.py, tables in results/heavy-final.txt. Component units are the paths pu-value-diff returns for each value write against the snapshot (propagator.rkt:1657): (position . facet) for the attribute map (typing-propagators.rkt:447), or the key for flat compound cells. Declared input paths are read from the dependent-entry (propagator.rkt:2319-2324). Dependency edges: a fire in round r depends on any fire in round r−1 whose changed units meet its declared watched paths, the rule filter-dependents-by-paths applies (:1707). Coverage: 100% of fires in rounds >0 have a predecessor. diag.py: work/span with component edges 1.28/1.49 against cell edges 1.27/1.46. If edges inside a run are dropped, T divided by the sum of each run's heaviest fire is 3.18 on both files.
verdicts.power_check: Power row, homing by propagator id: count parallelism at K=8 is 4.06/3.96 (C7 got 4.08/4.19 with a pid hash), so the round structure is wide by count and the method can report parallelism. Time-weighted, the same row gives only 1.24–1.25/1.33–1.34, and its async bound is 1.26–1.28/1.48–1.49. The edge matcher discriminates where the network allows it: on bool-logic work/span is 2.77 with component edges against 2.42 with cell edges.

verdicts.question: Q3a. Per-cell against per-component fencing: how many fenced↔free alternations occur per S0 run on the critical path? Is C9-11's 'the alternation has as many global synchronizations as BSP has rounds' true on the corpus?
verdicts.amendment: The rounds-proportional claim fails on the corpus. Crossings on the critical causal chain: per-cell mean 0.47/0.44 per run, max 1 (31/27 per file); per-component mean 0.55/0.49, max 1 (36/30 per file). Simulating D.2 §6.3's schedule (free phase first, each phase run to quiescence, a fire placed in the first phase of its colour after its predecessors) gives 1.47/1.44 switches per run under per-cell fencing and 1.55/1.49 under per-component, max 2. That is 97/88 and 102/91 per file, against 214/185 BSP rounds. C9's own falsifier ('≤ 2 alternations per S0 run with type cells fenced') is met. C9-11's direction still holds: switches plus the 61–66 run-end detections come to about 0.75–0.8 of the BSP round count, which is not ≪ rounds. ESTIMATE: at 7.3–15 µs per park/wake (P0 §4; C6-5), about 100 switches cost 0.7–3 ms per heavy file, more than the 0.6–1.5 ms of free work there is to parallelize.
verdicts.evidence: MEASUREMENT (gran_analyze.py alternations(), same DAG as Q2; results/heavy-final.txt). The round-order proxy (C3's metric) gives 79/74 under per-cell fencing; C3 reported 82/69 on first-in-process runs.
verdicts.power_check: A self-test on synthetic chains gives FUFU=3, FFF=0, FUUUF=2. A random colouring (pid parity) on the same DAGs gives up to 6 (constraints) and 5 (type) alternations per run, so the ≤1–2 measured is a property of the real fences, not a ceiling of the counter.

verdicts.question: Q3b. What share of fires and of fire time is fenced per cell against per component (per component = only the attribute map's :type components plus the type cells)? Does component-granular fencing leave K>1 work (CL-4 direction (ii))?
verdicts.amendment: Per-cell (attribute map or type-cell output): fires 0.890/0.854, time 0.986–0.988/0.973–0.974. Per-component, static per propagator (optimistic for propagators that never write): fires 0.358/0.331, time 0.913–0.918/0.853–0.854. Per-fire delta oracle: time 0.897–0.903/0.829–0.831. Conservative variant: time 0.960–0.962/0.911–0.913. The fence covers almost the same time at either granularity, because the heavy fires are exactly the :type writers: 286/241 :type units written, against 8/22 other facets. Zero-overhead async bounds at K=8: per-cell home with per-cell fence 1.00/1.01; per-component with the static fence 1.04–1.05/1.08; with the delta fence 1.06/1.11. So whole-network K=1 (option i) gives up ≤1–2% of S0 fire time against the per-cell alternation, and ≤5–11% against per-component fencing (≤1.3% of command). C3-2/C10-2's point, that D.2's own D2P-5 rule picks option (i), holds at both granularities. Type cells proper contribute nothing in S0: the type meta universe, cell 32, is an output of 27 fires and is never written.
verdicts.evidence: MEASUREMENT (results/heavy-final.txt). Type cells were identified as: merge named type-unify-or-top or type-lattice-merge; or merge eq? to current-type-universe-merge (meta-universe.rkt:178, set at elaborator-network.rkt:1060); or cell id = current-type-meta-universe-cell-id (meta-universe.rkt:207); or a contradiction fn from elaborator-network.rkt (elab-fresh-meta, :138-144). The :type facet reaches type-unify-or-top through facet-merge (typing-propagators.rkt:401-406) and classify-inhabit.rkt:171.
verdicts.power_check: The classifier separates in both directions: under the per-fire delta it marks 17.8–19.5% of fires fenced and 80% free. The random-colouring row gives 0.48–0.55 of time fenced. The type-cell detector finds the type universe (cell 32, compound-tagged-merge closure decision-cell.rkt:582) where it exists. The merge census covers every S0 output merge: attribute-map, meta-solution, classify-inhabit-request, resolution-stratum, set-union, tagged :527, table-answer, compound :582, viability, worldview-cache.

verdicts.question: Q4. Do Q1–Q3 hold beyond the two heavy files, on ≥8 of the 19 medium-tier files (one per process)?
verdicts.amendment: All 17 non-heavy files were run, one per process, 5 timing reps each. 6 run no BSP S0 at all: church-folds, dependent-types, higher-order, pairs-sigma, pattern-matching, recursive-types. The other 11 have 6–150 fires and 0.009–0.395 ms of S0 fire time, 0.1–11% of the command; together, 1.47 ms of S0 fire over 127 ms of commands (1.2%). Per-cell K=8 busiest share by time is ≥0.75 on 9 of the 11 (parity-adversarial 0.34, atms 0.75). The per-component K=8 busiest share by time is 0.14–0.62. Per-round time parallelism, per component at K=8: 1.0–1.85. work/span: 1.0–2.77. Per-component fenced time on the elaboration files: 0.29–0.90. The solver files show 0: their S0 fires are attribute-map fires that write nothing, plus solver cells. D.2-schedule switches ≤2 per run. Time-weighted medium-tier async bounds at K=8: per-cell with per-cell fence 1.04; per-component with per-component fence 1.13; per-component without a fence 1.60; homing by pid 1.63. The relational and solver files (atms-adversarial 134 fires in 108 runs, solve-adversarial 77/77, solve-scale 6/6, parity-adversarial 62/21) run about one fire per S0 run, with ≤0.14 ms of S0 fire (≤0.5% of command). parity-adversarial raises 'solve: Depth limit exceeded (100)' out of process-file under the production executor as well, so its numbers cover the prefix before the raise.
verdicts.evidence: MEASUREMENT. bash run-all.sh 5 → out/*.json and out/run-all.log (load 3.1→3.8); gran_analyze.py → results/all.summary.json, results/table-all.txt, results/medium-aggregate.txt. coverage-check.rkt (out/coverage-check.out): on the 6 zero-fire files the elaborator's quiescence scheduler (metavar-store.rkt:1766) is entered 1–4 times, always with an empty worklist, and 0 of those entries are Tier-1-shaped. control-raise.rkt (results/control-raise.out) shows the parity-adversarial raise is the same with the production and the sequential executor.
verdicts.power_check: coverage-check on constraints-adversarial sees 1136 executor fires, so the executor instrument does see S0 work where it exists. The zero-fire files are real zeros, not blind spots, except Tier-1 flushes outside the elaborator entry (propagator.rkt:3431-3445), which the executor cannot see. Those are fire-once propagators with empty inputs. implicit-args reproduces C3 exactly (150 fires, 0.867).

verdicts.question: Verdict: does P3 have a workload under any ownership unit? (C10-6: defer K>1 to a sequel; CL-16 scope)
verdicts.amendment: C10-6 holds: there is no workload in the repo today for any unit (cell, component or propagator id) or any K in {4,8,16}. Best case (per-component or pid homing, no fence, zero coordination cost): S0 fire speedup ≤1.28/1.49 on the heavy files, which is ≤1.05/1.06 on the command since S0 fire is 0.22/0.17 of the command. With D.2's fence at component granularity: ≤1.05/1.08 S0, ≤1.01 command. Medium tier: ≤1.6× on 1.2% of command time. After P2-lite (one full pu-value-diff removed per compound write) S0 fire time falls 48%/40% and work/span is unchanged (1.27–1.29/1.47–1.49), so P3's absolute target shrinks further. ESTIMATE: the median S0 run does 54–63 µs of fire work; one semaphore wake (7.3–15 µs) plus ~1.5 fence switches per run eat more than the ≤12–20 µs a 1.28–1.49× bound could save on it. The one place with slack is across S0 runs: the largest run is 8–11% of S0, so T over the max run is 9–12. CONJECTURE: that slack is reachable only by command- or definition-level parallelism. Inter-run dependencies were not measured. What would change this: a program whose S0 runs show work/span ≥3 and S0 share ≥30% (BSP-LE 3 search on the network is the named candidate). gran-probe.rkt measures any .prologos file without a rebuild.
verdicts.evidence: Synthesis of Q1–Q4 (results/heavy-final.txt, results/medium-aggregate.txt). Amdahl inputs: S0 fire share 0.218–0.229 and 0.168–0.178 of median command wall (timing reps, no observer). Bounds: 1/(1−0.22·(1−1/1.28)) = 1.05; 1/(1−0.17·(1−1/1.49)) = 1.06. Per-run S0 fire: p50 0.063/0.054 ms, max 0.84/0.81 ms.
verdicts.power_check: The bounds are upper bounds (zero overhead, perfect placement, BSP's own dependency DAG) and are reported next to the power rows (pid homing) that reach the same cap. The cap is not an artifact of the probe: with intra-run edges removed it rises to 3.18, so the instrument can show parallelism the dependencies do not allow.

findings.section: D.2 §2 item 3 (K>1 models 4.07×/3.26×), §6.7 Ownership, §16 R-1; triage CL-1 direction
findings.claim_attacked: The hub cell and the home rule are what limit K>1, so making the component the unit of ownership (CL-1's direction) recovers the modelled parallelism.
findings.evidence: On the heavy files, per-component ownership gives a busiest share by time of about 1/K (0.14 at K=8), but time-weighted parallelism is 1.19/1.35 per round. The zero-overhead async bound is work/span = 1.28/1.49 at any K, and pid homing (perfect balance) gives the same. In each round one :type fire holds 69–79% of the round's time, and those fires form a chain (3.0–3.2 rounds per run on average). Component edges rather than cell edges change work/span only from 1.27 to 1.28 and from 1.46 to 1.49.
findings.direction: Replace D.2 §2 item 3's models, which assume every fire is parallel (fire time / min(width, K)), with a work/span model computed from the dependency DAG (gran_analyze.py). State P3's value as min(K, work/span, 1/busiest-share) × the S0 share. Read P3's entry gate from this instrument rather than from ownership balance.
findings.falsifier: A corpus file where gran-probe.rkt measures work/span ≥3 within S0 runs, with S0 fire ≥30% of the command.

findings.section: D.2 §2 item 2, §6.6; triage CL-16 (C10-3)
findings.claim_attacked: P2 (DIRECT) is the main sequential lever; C10-3's P2-lite (a keyed diff) is an ESTIMATE.
findings.evidence: An independent instrument corroborates C10-3. Timing pu-value-diff on every live (snapshot, result) pair of a compound write, min of 5, and removing one diff per written compound cell per fire, removes 4.90–4.99 ms of 10.02–10.44 ms of S0 fire time (48%) on constraints-adversarial and 2.92–2.98 of 7.32–7.54 ms (40%) on type-adversarial. That is about 22 µs per attribute-map write, against C10's 23.8 µs. It is a lower bound on the in-fire diff cost, because a fire that writes k facets through k that-writes pays k diffs (net-cell-write's component-path diff, propagator.rkt:2042-2072). It is not a command-time measurement; W2-2 owns that.
findings.direction: Let W2-2's keyed-diff leg be the command-time check. Treat the per-write diff as the first cost to absorb at K=1. Note that it shrinks the absolute target of K>1 while leaving work/span unchanged (1.27–1.29/1.47–1.49).
findings.falsifier: W2-2's keyed-diff leg showing < 20% less S0 fire time on the heavy files.

findings.section: D.2 §1 scope, §6.8; W2-8's proposed first targets (relational and solver files)
findings.claim_attacked: The relational and solver workloads in the repo are S0 workloads that K>1 could target first.
findings.evidence: 6 of the 19 comparative files run no BSP S0: the elaborator's quiescence scheduler only ever sees empty worklists (coverage-check.out). The relational and solver files run about one fire per S0 run: atms-adversarial 134 fires in 108 runs, solve-adversarial 77/77, solve-scale 6/6, parity-adversarial 62/21. Their S0 fire time is 0.009–0.141 ms, 0.1–0.5% of the command, and solve-adversarial's 77 fires write nothing. Across the 17 non-heavy files S0 fire is 1.2% of command time.
findings.direction: Cite these numbers in the CL-16 scope decision. A K>1 target must be a workload that does not exist yet (BSP-LE 3 search on the network), which supports C10-6's sequel.
findings.falsifier: A test or example in the repo whose S0 fire time is >30% of its command with work/span ≥3, measured by gran-probe.rkt.

findings.section: P0 census baselines; triage CL-1 replication table
findings.claim_attacked: Per-file fire counts (P0's census 1142/1112, C3) are properties of the file.
findings.evidence: The first file processed in a process does different S0 work. Without a preload: 1142 fires/212 rounds and 1112/182 on the first rep, then 1136/214 and 1140/185 on reps 2–3. With a preload: 1136/214 and 1140/185 on every rep. The executor (production or sequential) makes no difference (results/fire-count-check.out). Separately, parity-adversarial raises 'solve: Depth limit exceeded (100)' out of process-file under both executors (results/control-raise.out), so any timing of that file measures only the prefix before the raise.
findings.direction: Pin a preload, or state first-in-process, in every per-file count used as a baseline. Flag parity-adversarial's raise in the medium-tier harnesses.
findings.falsifier: The same counts on the first and later reps without a preload.

W2-2.summary: I made one scratch build (git archive of 07fe9a12, whose racket/prologos is identical to df80be74) with five switches set by environment variables. They turn off the thread executor (EXEC_OFF), turn on the keyed diff (KEYED_DIFF) and the delta-carried writes (DELTA_WRITES), and run the equivalence monitors and their power rows. The legs were timed in two schedules: A–D × 8 rounds, then A–E × 8 rounds. Each round used rotated leg order, held the suite lock and ran 18 comparative files with 5 reps per process. Turning off the thread executor saves about 35 % on the two heavy files (≈22–25 ms each) and about 22 % on the medium tier. The keyed diff matches the full diff on all 2992 eligible writes (0 mismatches); its power row (drop one key) is caught on 1980 writes. Its speedup is 1.47–1.49× / 1.23–1.27× with the executor off, but only 1.13–1.23× with it on. Delta-carried writes fitted in bounded time and were built. With all three changes the heavy files run 3.45× / 2.52× faster than today and the medium tier 1.65×. They are not exactly equivalent: 2 of 1034 carried writes merged to a different value (an unsolved-meta classifier). From one instrument (the main-thread sampler, executor off), P2 would still give 3.2–3.3× / 2.0–2.1× over the build with the executor off and the keyed diff on, but only about 1.07–1.22× after delta-carried writes; by then about 2/3 of command time is outside BSP. Printed program outputs could not detect a deliberately wrong diff, so a per-write monitor is the only instrument for equivalence that has power.

verdicts.question: Q1. How much command time does removing the thread executor save on the two heavy files, and on the medium tier?
verdicts.amendment: Quantified. The saving is concentrated in files with wide BSP rounds. 11 of the 16 non-heavy files are at parity (0.96–1.05), so P0.5 is a ~1.5× win on the heavy files and ~1.08× on the rest. About 7 ms of the heavy-file saving is GC: the GC time inside each heavy run drops from 8 ms to ≤1 ms.
verdicts.evidence: MEASUREMENT. Command time is the wall time of process-file after an in-process preload (w22-time.rkt): the median over 8 interleaved processes of each process's median of 5 reps, under the suite lock (hold-suite-lock.rkt). Load is `uptime` 1-min: t1 2.49–3.87, t2 3.75–7.01. Leg A = as-is, B = W22_EXEC_OFF=1 (driver.rkt:567 is skipped, so BSP falls back to sequential-fire-all through the #:executor default at propagator.rkt:3401). Results, A→B: constraints-adversarial 66.3→44.1 ms (t1; range A 63–67, B 43–46) and 71.5→46.8 (t2); type-adversarial 63.5→40.9 (t1) and 67.1→43.1 (t2). The heavy pair summed: 129.9→85.0 (0.654) and 138.5→90.0 (0.649). Medium tier, 18 files: 245.4→192.2 (0.783) and 259.6→202.6 (0.780). The other 16: 115.5→107.2 (0.928) and 121.1→112.6 (0.930). Per-file B/A: implicit-args 0.52–0.54, bool-logic 0.60–0.63, scheduler-adversarial 0.72–0.77, nat-arithmetic 0.74–0.78, records-seal-validate 0.81–0.85; the rest 0.96–1.05. S0 fire-ms (current-bsp-round-stats): 27.1→10.6 and 23.9→7.4. The GC time inside each heavy run drops from 8 ms to ≤1 ms. This reproduces C2's 63 vs 42 ms. Command: `LEGSET="A B C D" hold-suite-lock.rkt suite-lock.rkt bash round.sh r OUT` for r = 0..7, then `summarize.py t1/legs.jsonl`.
verdicts.power_check: Every JSON row carries `executor_installed` (true in A and C, false in B and D), so the switch is verified per process, not assumed. The two independent schedules agree within 0.005 on every tier ratio. The per-process total ranges do not overlap on the heavy files (A 126.9–161.4 vs B 82.8–97.4 ms). The same method resolves the 7 % effect on the 16-file subset. The parity files have S0 fire-ms ≈ 0, so no executor effect is expected there: the null result has a mechanism, not just a lack of resolution.

verdicts.question: Q2. Is the keyed diff's output identical to the full diff on every write? (equivalence monitor + power row)
verdicts.amendment: It holds for every merge registered key-preserving; today that is attribute-map-merge-fn, which covers 2992 of the 3072 diffs (97.4 %). Other merges must keep the full diff unless they satisfy the hypothesis. Two caveats. (1) Under BSP's whole-map write in bulk-merge-writes, the keyed diff walks every key and saves nothing there; it pays only on in-fire writes and on writes outside BSP. (2) End-to-end output equality is not a valid substitute for the monitor (see power_check).
verdicts.evidence: THEOREM. Hypothesis H: for a merge m, every key k outside keys(new) has m(old,new)[k] eq? old[k] (old keeps every such key). Under H, pu-value-diff(old, m(old,new)) equals, as a multiset, the same per-key logic restricted to keys(new). Proof: pu-value-diff (propagator.rkt:1657-1694) skips eq? values in its first loop. Its removed-key loop can only fire on keys of new, because H keeps every other key of old. attribute-map-merge-fn (typing-propagators.rkt:447-470) folds from old and only hash-sets keys of new, so H holds. Its non-hash arms either return new (the keyed diff is guarded off when old is not a hash) or return old (an eq? no-change exit, where no diff is computed). MEASUREMENT. A full monitor (W22_KEYED_MONITOR=full) computes both diffs on every eligible slow-path write, compares them as multisets and returns the full diff. Over 19 files, one per process: eligible 2992, compared 2992, mismatches 0 with the executor off (mon/mon-execoff.jsonl). With the executor on it is again 2992/0 (mon/dw-execon.jsonl; the counters use box-cas!). Of the eligible writes, 2226 had a written value smaller than the map; there the full diff walks 1,121,184 keys and the keyed diff 63,592. 766 were whole-map writes (bulk). Command: `./monitor.sh mon/mon-execoff.jsonl W22_EXEC_OFF=1`.
verdicts.power_check: Power row: W22_KEYED_POWER=1 makes the keyed diff drop the first key of the written value. The monitor flags 1980 of 2992 writes, in every one of the 9 files that has eligible writes (e.g. constraints 878/1324, type 745/1146; mon/power-execoff.jsonl). The uncaught ~1012 are whole-map writes and writes whose dropped key did not change. Second power test, end to end: the same wrong diff returned to the scheduler (leg P, monitor off) changed NO deterministic file's printed-result fingerprint (17/17 SAME, pw/legs.jsonl). type-adversarial's output already differs between runs within leg A. W2-3.summary: I built one exhaustive model (`w23_model.py`) with K = 2–3 executors and a detector. Every load and store is its own step, and the model runs under SC, TSO store buffering and PSO (stores to different addresses may reorder, as on ARM without a release). It includes local cascades, counted, uncounted or missing fire requests, a contradiction stop with three boundary rules, regions keyed by network id, and the late-write check. In it, D.2's detector declares early in 22 steps at K = 2 and in 35 steps at K = 3, under every memory model. On a new CASCADE row of a real microbenchmark, D.2's detector also declared early in 7 of 7 trials at K = 2, 4 and 8, against 0 of 7 on P0's CHAIN and BURST rows. Every repair (a)–(e) is sound only if fire requests are counted messages, and live after a contradiction only if the boundary fires on quiescence or contradiction and executors park in a handshake. D.1's flag fails if the detector reads its words in another order, which ARM permits, unless the ack is deferred; the parity counter, the quiet mark, the deferred ack and credit are robust to read order. The smallest sound repair is (d) taken to its end: the epoch's seeds are counted messages, cons_i is published only when the cascade has drained, there is no idle indicator, and the detector is one pass that reads every cons and then every prod, so the double scan goes. Under store buffering it needs no fences; on ARM it needs one release per idle transition, plus prod stored before the lane publish, which `detect.rkt`'s `send!` already orders. Measured under the suite lock, it costs the same as D.2's own scheme within noise (CHAIN 86/107/220 vs 89/106/224 ns/msg at K = 2/4/8), while credit recovery costs 16–50× more on chains.

verdicts.question: Q1. Reproduce, in one model of your own, the premature declaration in D.2's detector (idle-epoch max-counter, Σprod = Σcons, two scans).
verdicts.amendment: The defect does not depend on the memory model: the same 22-step trace exists under SC. P0 §4.1 had no power to see it, because its rows contain no local cascade.
verdicts.evidence: MEASUREMENT (exhaustive interleaving). Command: cd <scratch>/d3w2/W2-3 && timeout -k 10 600 python3 w23_run.py q1 power > w23_q1_power.out. Output: 'CASCADE D2 SC states=5456 PREMATURE STALE'; TSO states=23450 PREMATURE; PSO states=59654 PREMATURE; 'K3 D2 SC states=877246 PREMATURE' (35-step witness). K = 2 witness: B goes idle (ind=1); A fires p, sends a delta to B (prod=1) and goes idle (ind=1); B drains the delta, writes cB and publishes cons=1, and q1→q2 is still queued; both scans read PA=1 CA=0 IA=1 PB=0 CB=1 IB=1 → DECLARE. verdicts.question: Q2(a). D.1's resettable flag: sound? live? fences? monotone state?
verdicts.amendment: It is sound when cons is published after the cascade. That is D.1 §5.4:136's 'cons = received **and processed**' read literally (my variant FLAGD), and it is what detect.rkt does (:115-126, where cons is stored after the drain's sends). Under that reading the flag is redundant: the deferred ack alone is sound (see Q2(d)). If cons is published at the join instead (D.2's ack point), the flag is sound only for particular store and load orders. It fails when cons is stored before the flag, and when the detector reads prod, flag, cons. It also fails under unordered reads, by ABA (busy, then idle again, between two reads of the same flag). SC-14's 'detect.rkt's resettable-flag scheme, which is sound' is right, but for the wrong reason: the ack point carries the soundness, not the flag.
verdicts.evidence: MEASUREMENT. FLAG (ack at drain) is sound+live on CASCADE, SENDWRITE, FREQ, BOUNCE, SEEDS2 and K3 at SC and TSO, read order PCI (w23_matrix.out; K3 TSO states=4583115). Failures (w23_q1_power.out, w23_supplement.out): 'BOUNCE FLAG SC read=PIC PREMATURE' (27-step ABA witness); 'BOUNCE FLAG SC read=ANY PREMATURE'; 'BOUNCE FLAG TSO read=ANY PREMATURE'; 'CASCADE FLAG SC pub=cons-ind PREMATURE'. FLAGD (w23_flagd.out) is sound+live on all 5 workloads with all six fixed read orders and with read=ANY, at SC and TSO, and under PSO with fences pub+send; CONTRA with the QCH boundary is sound+live. Fences: TSO none. On ARM, one release between flag:=busy and cons, and one before flag:=idle; the 'PSO -' rows are PREMATURE. Monotone: prod and cons are max-counters. The flag is a reset cell, which is not monotone. Its non-monotonicity is what the detector reads.
verdicts.power_check: Each failing variant differs from a passing one in exactly one store order or read order, so the engine separates them. The same read=ANY runs are sound for ACT, QUIET, DEFER, SEEDS and CREDIT.

Microbench mode act: CHAIN 110/159/302 ns/msg, CASCADE 539/750/1519 (detect-w23.out, which still has the head-store artefact).

verdicts.amendment: It needs counted fire requests. On ARM it needs a release before each cons store and before each mark store.
verdicts.evidence: MEASUREMENT. Sound+live: 5 workloads at SC/TSO/PSO+pub; K3 SC (1 333 008 states); all six fixed read orders on BOUNCE; read=ANY on 5 workloads at SC/TSO (BOUNCE TSO ANY: 2 907 390 states). verdicts.question: Q2(d). cons published only after the cascade drains (C1, C5): sound? live? fences? monotone state? Is it the smallest sound repair?
verdicts.amendment: Take (d) to its end and it becomes the smallest sound repair: SEEDS with a one-pass detector. The epoch's seeds are counted messages on a scheduler lane. prod_i is stored before the lane publish, and cons_i only when the worklist is empty. No idle indicator is needed. The detector reads every cons_j, then (acquire) every prod_j, and declares iff the sums are equal, with no second scan and no memory between scans. That removes D.2's stable-twice and answers C1-4's statelessness point without credit's arithmetic. DEFER (D.2's sticky idle-epoch with the ack deferred) is also sound; it is the smallest diff to D.2's text, but it keeps a redundant word.
verdicts.evidence: THEOREM. Hypotheses: (H1) all S0 work in an epoch is caused by counted messages (seeds, deltas, fire requests); (H2) prod_i is incremented and published before the message is visible; (H3) cons_i grows by the messages consumed only when the executor's worklist is empty, after those messages' effects are visible; (H4) prod and cons are monotone; (H5) the detector reads all cons, then all prod. Claim: equal sums ⇒ the system was quiescent at time T, between the last cons read and the first prod read, and stays quiescent. Proof: H2 and H3 give Σcons(t) ≤ Σprod(t) at every instant. H4 gives Σcons_read ≤ Σcons(T) ≤ Σprod(T) ≤ Σprod_read, so equality forces Σcons(T) = Σprod(T). By H3 every acked cascade is complete. By H1 every busy executor holds an unacked message, so nothing is busy or in flight at T. ∎ MEASUREMENT (w23_onepass.out): SEEDS CSPLIT scans=1 is sound+live on CASCADE, SENDWRITE, FREQ, BOUNCE and SEEDS2 at SC, TSO and PSO(pub+send); on K3 at SC and TSO (87 536 states); in the LOG layout under PSO+pub; with CONTRA QCH, REGIONS upstream-first and NESTED. Two-scan SEEDS: K3 TSO 581 824 states and K3 PSO(pub+send) 549 274, both sound+live. DEFER: K3 TSO 4 487 052 and K3 PSO(pub+send) 4 983 244, both sound+live. Fences: TSO none (every '-' row at TSO is sound). On ARM: one release before the cons store, once per idle transition. 'SENDWRITE SEEDS PSO fences=send' is STALE, so this release is needed for the handler to see the writes. The prod-before-lane order is also needed ('PSO pub' without send: PREMATURE or STALE), and detect.rkt's send! already provides it: prod is stored before the slot, then release, then tail (:34-39, :61-62). Detector: one acquire between the two passes. Monotone cells: prod_i and cons_i are max-counters (or derived reads under LOG). Executor-private scratch, labelled as realization: unacked_i, the worklist, read cursors. In DEFER, idle-epoch is a max-counter.
verdicts.power_check: Four mutants of the one-pass detector each fail (w23_onepass.out): prod read before cons ('BOUNCE SEEDS SC scans=1 PCI PREMATURE', 11 steps); counting after the publish ('SENDWRITE SEEDS SC CSPLIT lane-prod PREMATURE', 14 steps); acking at drain (EARLY: 'CASCADE EARLY SC scans=1 CSPLIT PREMATURE', 7 steps; two scans also PREMATURE); PSO without the send-side order ('SENDWRITE SEEDS PSO pub CSPLIT PREMATURE', 20 steps).

verdicts.question: Q2(e). Credit recovery with a monotone threshold (C1; Mattern 1989; Huang 1989): sound? live? fences? monotone state?
verdicts.amendment: It is sound and live, and it is the only scheme whose global decision is a monotone threshold read in a single scan. It is not the smallest repair. Exact dyadic credit costs 16–50× per message on chains, because credit halves per hop and k reaches 20 000 bits; Huang's alternative is a borrow protocol with a controller. It also cannot be keyed by region: a cross-region message carries no credit of the destination region, so per-region closure is premature even when upstream regions close first.
verdicts.evidence: MEASUREMENT. Sound+live: 6 workloads at SC/TSO/PSO+pub (K3 TSO 11 448 states); read=ANY on 5 workloads; CONTRA QCH under PSO with the park release. Power: uncounted fire requests PREMATURE, missing ones WRONGFIX; 'PSO -' STALE; CONTRA with the counters-only boundary NOT-LIVE; with QC (no handshake) RACE. Regions (w23_supplement.out S3): 'REGIONS CREDIT SC tasks=[(2,),(1,)] PREMATURE' (17-step witness: B returns its region-2 credit, then RA[r1]=1 → DECLARE (1,) with the region-2 → region-1 delta in flight). Counters close the same order soundly. Cost (detect-w23.out, WORK=20): CHAIN 5368/4193/4493 ns/msg against seeds1 105/141/272 in the same run; BURST 729/239/152 against 33/31/62. Monotone: returned_i is an exact sum with one writer; held credit is scratch; message credit travels in the lane.

verdicts.question: Q2-FR. Counted fire requests for dependents homed elsewhere (D.1 §5.3, dropped by D.2's Lane = Set [CellId Delta]).
verdicts.amendment: Every repair, credit included, needs dependents homed elsewhere to be woken by counted lane messages. Lane must carry (propagator, wake) beside (cell, delta).
verdicts.evidence: MEASUREMENT (w23_q1_power.out). FREQ with fr=uncounted: D2, FLAG, ACT, QUIET, DEFER, SEEDS and CREDIT are all PREMATURE (SEEDS: 15-step witness). FREQ with fr=none: all WRONGFIX (SEEDS: 14 steps). K3 fr=uncounted/none (w23_q1_power.out from quick2 runs): FLAG, SEEDS and CREDIT PREMATURE / WRONGFIX. With counted requests, FREQ and K3 are sound+live for every repair (w23_matrix.out).
verdicts.power_check: The same workload passes with counted requests, so the fire-request mode alone flips the result.

verdicts.question: Q2-CONTRA. The contradiction stop: does any repair stay live, and what must the boundary be?
verdicts.amendment: The boundary must fire on (quiescent ∨ contradiction) with a parking handshake. Each executor stores parked_i after a release; the handler reads cells only after every parked_i is set. Messages in flight at the stop are discarded with the epoch. Two items are not modelled: the contradiction payload as a set (C5-8), and an exception becoming a contradiction plus a park (C6-4); by construction the second is a QCH row.
verdicts.evidence: MEASUREMENT (w23_contra_regions_late_log.out, w23_supplement.out S3). With the counters-only boundary (Q), SEEDS, DEFER, FLAG, CREDIT and D2 are NOT-LIVE at SC, TSO and PSO; the initial state can never reach the boundary. With QC (no handshake), all are RACE at SC/TSO/PSO (SEEDS SC: 10-step witness, a write of cB after the handler starts). With QCH: sound+live at SC and TSO for all; under PSO, park+pub+send is sound+live for SEEDS, DEFER, FLAG and CREDIT, and pub+send without park is RACE for all four. The LOG layout with QCH and park+pub is sound+live. Fence count: TSO none; ARM one release per executor per boundary, not per message.
verdicts.power_check: Removing only the park release flips QCH under PSO to RACE.

verdicts.question: Q2-REGIONS. Nested regions keyed by network id.
verdicts.amendment: Keys by network id are necessary for the boundary/late-write state and for concurrent regions, but not sufficient. A region may close only when its own sums balance AND every upstream region is complete (SCC order; PPN GR-6, BC-4). That condition is a monotone set of completed regions. For sequential nesting (a fork run from a boundary handler), process-wide counters are enough.
verdicts.evidence: MEASUREMENT. NESTED (region 1's handler seeds region 2): SEEDS and DEFER are sound+live keyed and unkeyed, at SC and TSO. With the late-write tag, 'tag=process' flags the correct nested run's writes ('late:CAUGHT', spurious), while per-network tags are 'late:clean' (C9-10 confirmed). REGIONS (region 2 sends into region 1): closing region 1 first is PREMATURE, WRONGFIX and STALE for SEEDS, DEFER, FLAG and CREDIT, at SC and TSO (SEEDS: 19-step witness). Closing region 2 first is sound+live for the counter schemes but PREMATURE for CREDIT. Unkeyed global detection is sound+live.
verdicts.power_check: Region order alone flips the result for the counter schemes.

verdicts.question: Q3a. The late-write check (C5-7): with the chosen detector, is write-then-check with fences needed, or a parking handshake?
verdicts.amendment: Use the parking handshake at every boundary. Demote 'late-s0-write to an executor-local assertion, 'no fire while parked', which needs no fence. With a sound detector no S0 write can follow a quiescence declaration, so write-then-check has nothing to catch. Making it a monitor that can catch a detector bug needs a store→load fence on both sides, that is, a full fence per S0 cell write. Racket CS documents memory-order-release as at least a store–store and store–load fence (Reference memory-order.scrbl:41-42); memory-order-acquire is not a store→load fence (:38-39), so C6's 0-count acquire row in the SB litmus is an observation, not a guarantee. This closes R-2 as C6-3 proposed.
verdicts.evidence: MEASUREMENT (w23_contra_regions_late_log.out, run against the unsound D2 detector so that late writes exist). SC: CTW (check, then write) → 'late:CAUGHT/MISSED/clean', i.e. it misses even under SC; WTC → no MISSED. TSO: CTW, WTC, WTC with a detector fence, and WTCF (writer fence only) all reach MISSED; only WTCF with a detector fence has no MISSED. This reproduces C5-7 inside the full detector model. With sound detectors, CASCADE SEEDS TSO, CASCADE DEFER TSO, K3 SEEDS SC (192 496 states) and K3 DEFER SC (923 583 states) all give 'late:clean' only. Contradiction boundaries need the handshake (see Q2-CONTRA).
verdicts.power_check: Against D2 the same check reports CAUGHT and MISSED, so it can fire; it reports clean only against sound detectors.

verdicts.question: Q3b. Do lanes modelled as logs with cursors, so that prod and cons are derived reads (C4-8), remove the ordering invariant between separate cells?

findings.claim_attacked: That a production run-to-quiescence result is a fixpoint of its own S0 propagators, so that a non-fixpoint or replay monitor reads 0 on correct runs and a re-run of S0 cannot change an answer. The NAF handler's comment says 'If provable → nogood for h_naf … tagged writes under h_naf become invisible' (relations.rkt:346-353).
findings.evidence:
MEASUREMENT. The S1 NAF handler process-naf-request (relations.rkt:206-354) records a NAF failure as an AND-NOT read-modify-write directly on the worldview cache, cell 1 (:240 per-binding path; :350-353 shared-bit path; the S0 guard does the same at :2346-2349, which is DEFERRED 157(b)). It does not write the decisions cell that cell 1 is projected from. Cell 1 has a second writer: the worldview projection propagator that make-solver-context installs on every query network (atms.rkt:237; propagator.rkt:978-987, which reads decisions cell 20 and writes cell 1 with a replacement merge). After the run, the projection's output disagrees with cell 1.
q3-tier1-sweep.rkt, over 76 ATMS query networks built on the production path, flags 12 results, all from relations with `not` goals: safe-twohop, safe-reach, fruit-not-of-color(2), light-vehicle, unreachable-from-a, reachable, ancestor-e. In each, propagator 0 would change cell 1.
q3-cell1.rkt on examples/2026-07-19-rel-t1-acceptance.prologos `light-vehicle` (`&> (vehicle v) (not (license v))`): cell 1 is 0b11 after the run and 0b111 after one re-fire of propagator 0. Answers from the result: `{v0: "bicycle"}`, which equals DFS and production. Answers after S0 re-fires propagator 0: `{"automobile"} {"bicycle"}`, an answer DFS rejects.
The in-run detector also flags such states at round entry (forced ATMS: 2 in rel-t1, 2 in foray), i.e. while S0 continues after the S1 handler. Today's answers are right only because nothing re-fires the projection once the handler has run. None of the 12 queries that auto routes to ATMS in the repo hit it (0 flags under auto).
findings.direction: Write invalidation as growth, the way DEFERRED 157's measured fix shape does, extended to the S1 handler. NAF and guard verdicts go into an `ior` invalidated-bits cell, or are written as nogoods into the decisions cell that the projection reads. The projection propagator then derives worldview = committed ∧ ¬invalidated, so cell 1 has one writer and the S1 result is a fixpoint. This is the same split as CL-6's 'cell 1 becomes a derived projection α(decisions, nogoods)'. After the change, the generic detector must read 0 on the 12 flagged queries and light-vehicle must stay `{bicycle}` after a forced re-fire. PAR 4's replay/non-fixpoint monitor needs this before it can have a zero baseline on solver networks, and at K > 1 or under DIRECT an interleaving that re-fires the projection after the handler would produce the wrong answer.
findings.falsifier: A run in which re-firing propagator 0 after the S1 handler leaves cell 1 unchanged for a provable NAF goal. Or a proof that no scheduler PAR 4 plans (DIRECT, K > 1, the replay) ever fires the projection again after the S1 handler within one query.
findings.confidence: high (mechanism and the light-vehicle flip); medium (production reach: latent today)

W2-6.summary: The five CL-6 proposals are consistent with each other, and each is needed, but only with four amendments that wave 1 does not state. I built a lattice-level model on the real substrate (net-cell-write auto-tagging, promote-cell-to-tagged, BSP and the drain). With all of them in place — the ev_W read (a), a flat per-key ⊤ (row 2), unify-fire writing both sides (e), no network-wide viewpoint (b), and lifting with labelled outputs (c) — it gives DFS's answers on 8/8 rows under 3 schedules. Dropping any one part breaks at least one row (rows still right: 5/8, 2/8, 7/8, 6/8, 6/8). DEFERRED 177's filed fix ((a)+row 2+(e)) fixes its own three rows but not two more wrong-answer shapes I found on the shipped solver: `(pick ?x) (pick ?y) (= ?x ?y)` LOSES {x 2, y 2}, and `(pick ?x) (= ?x 2)` returns {x 1} {x 2} {x 1}. Both also need (b) and (c). (b) as written (delete cell-1 as the fallback viewpoint) would break elaboration's commit-by-keeping-the-bit (meta-universe.rkt:257-263; test-speculation-bridge.rkt:69-88). It would also send speculative networks into the Tier-1 flush (DEFERRED 178). The repair: a grow-only premise set P, read as W_p ∪ P; cell-1 retired as the tag source; Tier-1 dispatch on α. C8-5's anti-monotone guard mask comes from encoding nogoods as worldview bits. With nogood environments the same decision kills 0/144 passing rows, against 24/144 with bits. So (d) becomes: live and answers are read only over completed nogoods. D.2's two-phase set survives only as the codomain of the derived projection α = (C, X), which is monotone over 1 115 steps and whose live read equals today's cell-1. It does not survive as a cell with writers. Of cell-1's 11 production writers, one (make-branch-pu) is dead. test-tagged-cell-value.rkt:210-224 must flip. test-solver-context.rkt:341-362 need not: it is the regression catcher, failing under D.2's literal row 1 and passing once the viewpoint is per query. The existing DFS↔ATMS parity suite has no conflicting-binding case. A scratch extension with these rows fails 5/7 at HEAD in 0.2 s, and is the test layer to land with the fix.

verdicts.question: Q1 (overall): are proposals (a)–(f) consistent with each other?
verdicts.amendment: They are consistent, and each part is needed. Four amendments: (A1) (b) must not simply delete the fallback viewpoint. An unlabelled S0 fire reads at W_p ∪ P, where P is a grow-only set of committed premises, because elaboration commits a speculation by keeping its bit (elab-speculation-bridge.rkt:305-309). Only live = C ∧ ¬X is banned inside S0. (A2) (b) must also retire cell-1 as the TAG source in net-cell-write (propagator.rkt:2011-2017) and net-cell-write-widen (:4065-4069). Otherwise an unconditional write made after any assumption is labelled with all of them, which is the R6 mechanism. BSP's Tier-1 dispatch (:3410, `(zero? worldview)`) must read 'assumptions exist' from α. (A3) '⊤ ⇒ nogood' is a property of the READ, not of a stored entry. In 177's row 2 the base is {x a} and the entry is {x b}; no entry is ⊤, but ev_W is. The rule is: ev_W has a ⊤ component ⇒ nogood(W), detected at the boundary read or by a lifted check fire. (A4) (c) is one rule. Each output entry is labelled with the W its inputs were read at (soundness). The fire is evaluated at every W a boundary will query, or once per input label when it is additive (completeness). Evidence that each part is needed (model rows that go wrong when it is dropped): (a): R2, R6, R7. Row 2: 6 rows, and R5 becomes schedule-dependent. (e): R3. (b): R6, R7. (c): R5, R8.

verdicts.question: Q1(a) :usage: with ⊥ standing for an unsolved multiplicity, are + and · monotone and associative at every arity on the chain ⊥ < m0 < m1 < mw? Or is the interval lattice the right carrier?
verdicts.amendment: C4-6 holds, but its two-way dilemma leaves out a third option. On the chain, the extensions of the real prelude ops that are sound, monotone and associative are 4 for + and 3 for ·. Every one that keeps 0-absorption (⊥·m0 = m0) must also set ⊥·m1 = m0, which turns 'unknown' into 'unused' (a lower-bound-only reading). The only chain extension that keeps ⊥ open is the fully strict one, which is C4's second horn. On the flat order (the order of mult-lattice.rkt:49), the best sound abstraction of + (ω absorbs ⊥) is not associative; only strict + survives, while 0-absorbing · survives. The interval lattice is the smallest carrier tested that keeps 'open' distinct from 'unused' and is exact. A flat lift with strict + and 0-absorbing · is correct but coarser. C9's G1 is correct on the 3-element chain without ⊥, and so is its claim that a fold of monotone ops is monotone at every arity. Order independence additionally needs associativity and commutativity, and that is exactly what fails once ⊥ is added (C4's point).

defence.argument: (1) A K > 1 design exists that is correct without CL-3, CL-4 or CL-12, and it is the one the principles already name. DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.org:846-848 puts per-network parallelism at "work distribution within one BSP round, or Gauss-Seidel sub-round", and :798-800 keeps the scheduler's smarts to efficiency. In a frontier step, every queued fire reads the same snapshot, so dynamic placement is free and no ownership unit exists. Results are folded in pid order by the cells' own merges, so K cannot change the result, even for the non-join cells D.2 wanted to fence; there is nothing to fence. The empty worklist on the orchestrator is quiescence, so no detector is needed. Measured: identical results and per-round fingerprints at K = 4 and 8, against a mutant power row. (2) It pays where the workload is wide: 1.83–2.78× on S0 for productive frontiers of 6 000–30 000 fires, using real fire-and-collect-writes and bulk-merge-writes and nothing but an injected executor. The crossover is about 0.3–0.7 ms of fire work per step. Asynchrony would add ≤ 3 % on today's traces, so the cheap design captures essentially all the K > 1 value that today's DAGs contain. (3) The decision belongs to this track because P2 rewrites the S0 inner loop now. defence.design_that_would_make_it_pay:
Information flow.
(a) Cells. S0 cells are unchanged: the CHAMP stays primary (γ1), and there are no owned slots. Each S0 run's network carries one per-run input cell, s0-k (CL-11's per-run K), with default 1; the caller sets it (runner 1; LSP and CLI ≤ cores − 2; never oversubscribed, C6-5). A per-run frontier threshold W, in fires or estimated fire-µs, is scheduler data taken from a committed crossover table. It does not depend on K, so K never changes the schedule.
(b) Scheduler. P2's DIRECT loop reads its worklist. When the frontier is at least W, it takes one Jacobi step:
- every queued propagator fires against the same snapshot pointer;
- each fire's write deltas are folded into the network in pid order by the cells' merges;
- with K > 1 the fires are computed by K executors, each taking the next index from a CAS counter.
Otherwise the loop runs DIRECT as at K = 1. Quiescence is the orchestrator's empty worklist, and a contradiction is checked once per step.
(c) Executors. Either a make-parallel-thread-pool created once per process, with fresh Racket threads per step that inherit the parameterization exactly as today's executor does, or parked persistent workers that install a parameterization captured per step (CL-13's interim). No spinning, because of GC stop-the-world time (C6-5).
(d) Gates.
- Equality of results and per-step fingerprints at K ∈ {1, 4, 8, 16}, with a drop-one-result power row (w28-bspk.rkt's shape).
- ≥ 1.5× on S0 at K = 8 on a named wide workload class. Today that is the intersection-merge networks, which should replace bench-parallel-demos' union demos; later, user networks and BSP-LE 3.
- No change at K = 1.
(e) Order of value. P0.5 deletes the production executor. P2-lite's keyed diff and delta merges take the 52 % serial merge out of BSP-K's way. Batching commands (PPN 4C) gives elaboration wide frontiers.
(f) The sequel (C10-6) builds asynchronous DIRECT-K only if some workload shows a DAG critical path well below its round span, which none in the repo does. It would use component-keyed deltas from P2-lite as the lane payload.

defence.argument:
1. Speed is not the reason to keep P2.
- With the executor off and the keyed diff in place, P2 and P2-lite-full have about the same speed (C10's shares).
- P2-lite-full reaches that speed by rebuilding DIRECT's write path inside BSP: every fire logs the deltas it passes to net-cell-write. Fires return networks (fire-propagator :377-379), so the log is a new ambient channel on every write, the kind of fire context D.2 §6.5 and CL-13 are retiring.
- Each write is then merged twice, once against the snapshot inside the fire and once in bulk.
- DIRECT gets the same deltas by construction and merges once. The keyed diff, which both need, pays more under DIRECT, because every DIRECT write is a delta. In BSP's bulk path the written value is the whole post-fire map, so a keyed diff degenerates to the full one.

2. What P2 removes that P2-lite cannot.
- Lost updates from read-modify-write writers on non-join cells (R2, measured). At K = 1 DIRECT is serializable; BSP, with or without deltas, is not.
- The snapshot classification machinery: fire-and-collect-writes' value / undeclared / new-structure capture (:2897-2983) and bulk's direct-set branch (:3044-3070).
- The Tier-1 special case and its non-fixpoint defect (PD-2). Tier 1 is DIRECT without the dependent drain, so P2 subsumes it. PD-2 is fixed by deletion, not by a patch.
- The drain, a third S0 dynamics with no strata and no fire-once, which can map onto the K = 1 executor (`:execution :sequential` becomes K = 1).
- Under P2, production keeps one S0 dynamics plus the oracle. Under P2-lite it keeps BSP, Tier 1 and the drain. So C1-8's 'two dynamics to keep equivalent' is worse under P2-lite, not better.
- P2 also forces CL-7's latch: DIRECT cannot produce fire-results (C2-10), so 'productive' must become 'trigger held', one semantics for DIRECT, the replay and any K.

3. BSP is the right oracle because it is the cheapest canonical schedule of the semantics, and it stays well defined when the hypotheses fail.
- C1-8's own theorem shows the round trace is the unique fixpoint of the lifted operator G, so BSP is not a privileged scheduler but G's depth-ordered evaluation. GT-3 is satisfied.
- The lift cannot beat BSP's evaluation count, because the lower bound is BSP's fire set. Its stateless form is quadratic in depth (measured), and an O(D) form needs per-depth propagators (G-1) or off-cell state.
- An oracle earns its keep when a hypothesis fails: user networks (GT-6), fenced cells, a P1b miss. There BSP's snapshot gives every read, declared or not, the round-n value, so its rounds are deterministic.
- The lift's schedule-independence is itself conditional on E1 and joins. It went blind to DIRECT's E1 error in F5b and livelocked on a non-join cell in F7.
- After P0.5 deletes the tree path (150) and the in-fire structure capture (158), the oracle's inner loop is snapshot + fire + merge + latch + observer.
- C3-10's point makes rounds-on-request one BSP replay from a pointer at K = 1.

4. New evidence for the theorems both sides use.
- A poisoned re-fire census (powered by five fixture rows) found 0 / 2 901 fires depending on undeclared cells, 0 / 2 815 on undeclared component paths, and 0 impure fires, across 12 corpus files including both heavy files.
- So C5-4's E1 holds on today's corpus to that method's power. It is a lower bound: reads through ambient boxes and parameters are invisible to it (W2-5).
- BSP's rounds are therefore Kleene's on the corpus, modulo E2–E5, which P1b and P0.5 address.
